meaning.zh:
“搞砸了” 或 “失误”。

这个短语来源于 “screw up”，字面意思是把某物拧得过头，引申为把事情搞得一团糟、做出巨大错误。在日常用语中， "a screwup" 常用于形容某人做了一个重大的错误或搞砸了一件事情。
meaning.en: This phrase comes from "screw up," which literally means to over-tighten something, and figuratively means to mess something up badly. In everyday language, "a screwup" is often used to describe someone who has made a significant mistake or messed something up.

lines.en: That was a major screwup on his part.
lines.zh: 那是他犯的一个重大失误。

lines.en: We can't afford another screwup this time.
lines.zh: 这次我们不能再搞砸了。

lines.en: Every project has at least one screwup, but we learn from them.
lines.zh: 每个项目至少会有一次失误，但我们会从中学到东西。
